record.original_question: Is every triangle-free graph with no 3-connected subgraph 3-colorable?

evidence.quote: Addendum : Is it true that every graph that contains no triangle and no 3-connected subgraph is 3-colorable ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. Recall that:
- $G$ is triangle-free if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices (no subgraph isomorphic to $K_3$).
- $G$ is 3-connected if $|V(G)| \ge 4$ and for every set $S \subseteq V(G)$ with $|S| \le 2$, the graph $G - S$ is connected.
- $G$ is 3-colorable if there exists a map $c: V(G) \to \{1,2,3\}$ such that $c(u) \ne c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E(G)$.

Decide whether the following statement is true: every finite simple graph $G$ that is triangle-free and contains no 3-connected subgraph is 3-colorable.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of the question whether every triangle-free graph with no 3-connected subgraph is 3-colorable. Related results (Grötzsch's theorem for planar triangle-free graphs, structural studies of ISK4-free or K4-subdivision-free graphs, and series-parallel-type decompositions) appear in the literature, but no source clearly confirms or refutes this exact statement, so its current status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Grötzsch's theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Every triangle-free planar graph can be colored with only three colors.
status_evidence.claim: A classical 3-colorability result for triangle-free graphs exists in the planar case, but does not extend to all triangle-free graphs.

status_evidence.title: Triangle-free graphs that do not contain an induced subdivision of K4
status_evidence.snippet: If G is triangle-free and ISK4-free, then either G is series-parallel, or G contains K3,3, or G contains a wheel.
status_evidence.claim: Structural results exist for triangle-free graphs with restricted K4-subdivision/3-connectivity behavior, but they do not directly resolve 3-colorability under the stated hypothesis.
